scope: Fresh matched Claude Code / Bruhs Claude coding cohort on pinned robfig/cron v2. This constrained CLI profile tests coding and transport, not full product defaults or leadership. Prior Codex outcomes remain separate.
success: Native completion inside the declared budget; all frozen 66 top-level Go checks and observed nested cases pass with race detector; supplied tests and docs; unblinded operator diff acceptance. Code checks alone do not count as completed work.
intervention_policy: No corrective feedback, retries, repairs, prompt changes or model switches within the six planned cells. Preserve every timeout/failure/unstarted cell. Configuration preflights occur before campaign freeze and are retained separately.
configuration: Both paths use installed Claude Code 2.1.322, exact Sonnet 5.5 model, high effort, acceptEdits, safe-mode, restricted file tools, explicit Read/Write/Edit/Glob/Grep/Bash tools, no skills/Chrome/session persistence, and enabled Bash sandbox with command network domains empty. OAuth remains in existing host configuration/keychain; no credentials are archived. Common wrapper provides these settings to native and Bruhs SDK CLI. Bruhs retains its host system contract, but safe-mode/tool restriction suppresses app MCP/customizations, so this is not normal product-default coverage. Offline Go wrapper is provided; coding children/tool environments are not fully attested. Independent grading uses pinned Go and new private cache. Non-interactive permission policy: native Claude print mode returns denials; the Bruhs HTTP fixture immediately declines every permission request via /api/agent/approve with approved=false and no reason or coding guidance. Every denial is audited. No request is approved, and no interactive owner waiting time is left unanswered.
limits: One known public repository task; familiarity and training overlap unknown.
Actual CLI configuration is recorded, not a proof against adversarial sandbox escape or a uniform coding-child cache policy.
No Capy, T3, OpenCode, aider, connected-workspace, native UI or forge comparison in this cohort.
Reported subscription session cost is not billed cost; invoices, total machine cost and complete human time remain unknown.
Three paired repeats are diagnostic; this cohort cannot establish statistical superiority or erase the earlier Bruhs Codex timeout.
predecessor: campaign-03 retained all six cells, including three Bruhs timeouts waiting on unserviced permission prompts. That driver mismatch invalidates a comparative interpretation. This new declaration fixes only the fixture permission-response policy before any fresh coding cell; it does not change those original outcomes.
